Here’s what you need to know INQUIRER.net / 05:09 PM November 10, 2026 Share: MANILA, Philippines — Planning to vote in the 2028 elections but have yet to register? Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you complete your voter registration, including the qualifications, requirements and documents you need to prepare.
To register as a voter, applicants must meet the following qualifications:
Eligible Filipinos may file applications at their local Commission on Elections (Comelec) offices and designated registration sites.
The poll body is accepting applications for first-time registration, transfer of registration records, reactivation of deactivated records, and correction or updating of personal information.
Applicants must bring at least one valid identification document, along with its original copy and a photocopy.
The ID must bear the applicant’s photograph, full name and address. Comelec accepts the following documents:
An electronic Philippine Identification (ePhilID) may also be presented, provided it can be accessed through the eGovPH app.

Comelec reminds applicants that barangay residency certificates, community tax certificates or cedulas, police clearances and company IDs are not accepted as proof of identity or residency.
Applicants who do not have any of the accepted identification documents may instead be identified under oath by either:
Each registered voter or qualified relative may serve as a guarantor for up to three applicants only.
Applicants may register at the Office of the Election Officer (OEO) with jurisdiction over the area where they intend to register or update their registration records.
Other designated registration venues include satellite offices, mall registration sites, the Special Registration Anywhere/Anytime Program (SRAP) and the Registration Anywhere Program.
Registration sites are open from Tuesday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The sites are also open Saturdays and holidays, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Before visiting a registration site, applicants may download and complete the application form from the Comelec website. The form must be printed back-to-back on legal-size paper.

The applications will then undergo the necessary evaluation and approval process before applicants are officially included in the voters’ list.
